avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and pays to have them planted on sidewalks, in parks and on private land. It also funds the machinery and employee crews that do this work in the boroughs. At the same time, borough councils allow construction projects to deviate from the rules on trees and greening.

etapes.texte: City council awards two contracts to supply and plant 1,374 trees in seven boroughs, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expenditure is $2,456,590.55, taxes included.

The City pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional land until December 31, 2026. Pierrefonds-Roxboro, for its part, transfers $162,233.12 from the parks fund to buy trees and plants.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion on rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75 and sets aside $200,000 for blue-collar crews assigned to planting. Outremont awards the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including planting vegetation, for an expenditure of $800,416.17, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

etapes.titre: Land leased for a tree nursery
etapes.texte: The City leases plots in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for $100, so it can operate a transitional tree nursery there. The lease runs for 24 months starting May 1, 2026, and the property subsidy is estimated at $329,600.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit a progress report on October 31, 2026, its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its summary report and financial statements on March 31, 2027.
The 855 trees in lot 2 must be planted in spring 2027; watering, maintenance and replacement continue until the end of November 2029.
The lease for the transitional tree nursery ends on April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Contracts for snow removal and snow loading, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.
deneigement.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs mainly signed, extended and paid for contracts related to snow: turnkey snow removal from streets and sidewalks, rental of graders and tractor-loaders with operators, vehicle towing and spring street cleaning. Some boroughs also drew on their surpluses to cover expenses from the 2025-2026 winter, and others amended their by-laws targeting contractors who clear snow on private land.

etapes.titre: Snow removal at downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie assigned to companies the maintenance, cleaning and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises, square Dorchester, place du Canada, square Victoria and other locations. It also extended by one year the snow removal of the Quartier des Spectacles, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord approved an additional expense for the rental of an extra grader, and Saint-Léonard allocated $200,000 of surplus to staff and abrasives [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offered to city council to provide its own staff at the snow disposal site for loading.

The City extended by twelve months turnkey snow removal contracts in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, towing contracts and rentals of equipment with operator in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Ville-Marie and Anjou did the same for their tractor-loaders and grader.

Anjou amended the amount of fines in its by-law on snow removal from land by contractors, and Ahuntsic-Cartierville amended its by-law on snow removal and clearing. Saint-Léonard tabled a draft by-law requiring snow removal contractors working on industrial, commercial and institutional land to hold a permit.

aSurveiller.texte: The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.
Snow removal from roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest runs from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: The City is funding and carrying out work on its water networks: rehabilitating pipes in several boroughs, replacing lead service connections and rebuilding main pipes under downtown streets. It is also continuing the disinfection project at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, including construction of the oxygen production unit, and is contracting out routine maintenance of the plant to private companies. It is adopting loan by-laws to pay for this work.

etapes.texte: The City is increasing from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is used to finish building the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen production plant.

The City is awarding a series of contracts to rehabilitate secondary water mains using lining, without digging trenches, and to redo the pavement. The work affects streets in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève, Pierrefonds-Roxboro, Saint-Laurent, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Lachine, Le Sud-Ouest, Outremont, Verdun, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and Saint-Léonard.

etapes.titre: Lead service connections handed to boroughs
etapes.texte: Boroughs are offering city council to carry out the replacement of lead service connections themselves, including the portion located on private land, under by-law 20-030. The costs of work done on private property are billed to the owners.

The City is awarding contracts to rebuild a 500 mm water main along rue Guy and pipes on rue De Champlain, and to rehabilitate a 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord. It is adding funds to the contracts for rue de la Cathédrale and rue Saint-Antoine Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: Adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary waterworks and sewer networks, announced for October 19, 2026.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 planned from the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
Completion of the rehabilitation work on the rue de la Cathédrale water main postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.
Work on rue Guy expected to continue until December 2027.
Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant expected in 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system streamlining.

etapes.texte: The City is requesting financial assistance from the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The file describes a 900-metre trail crossing the park, with a footbridge about 150 metres long and a 12.7-hectare meadow [CG26 0121].

etapes.titre: Urban greenhouses handed to the borough
etapes.texte: The City approves a complex of research, training and community production greenhouses in the park's southwest sector, with a construction budget estimated at $2,185,000 [CG26 0124]. The urban agglomeration delegates the project to city council, which accepts the offer from the arrondissement of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension to carry it out.

The borough awards a company the contract to redevelop rue De Louvain, between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62 [CA26 14 0076]. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: Site electrical work and park maintenance
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract for the second phase of electrical streamlining work at the complexe environnemental: new power supply, transformer, backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture. It also entrusts two companies with general upkeep and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months.

The City extends by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor at the complexe environnemental; the compost is used, among other things, for landscaping the park [CG26 0320]. The borough then awards a contract worth $499,865.92 including taxes for supplying and installing the greenhouses [CA26 14 0163].

etapes.titre: Snow removal and second funding request
etapes.texte: The City extends by six months the contract for snow removal at the park, the TAZ and the soccer stadium. The borough authorizes the submission of a funding request to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, under the Véloce III program, for a bike lane and sidewalks on rue De Louvain Est.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the TAPU program, to which the City is submitting its request for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouse installation work must be completed by December 2026, according to the borough's file.
The greenhouses are set to be put into service in winter 2027.
The extended snow removal covers the period from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2027.
The park maintenance contracts run until October 31, 2028, and 26 hectares will be added in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
The rue De Louvain construction project includes a phase from May to October 2027 and a phase from May to August 2028.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.
grand-parc-ouest.enBref: This year, the City is maintaining and protecting the sectors of the Grand parc de l'Ouest. It adjusted a contract for the repair of heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, filed an application for an international designation related to the night sky at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and had two sectors listed in a registry of protected natural environments. It also awarded contracts for culvert reconstruction, snow removal, tree felling, and housekeeping.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. Buried stones, additional mortar, and a degraded culvert explain the increase, according to file 1255414002.

The City files the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. It commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping nighttime access open to the public.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector (429 ha) are listed in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité, with conservation plans. Elected officials also take note of the 2025 report on the areas.

The City awards contracts for snow removal on the service roads and parking lots of Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques, as well as housekeeping for nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, including the chalet d'accueil, Maison Richer, and Château Gohier.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with no possible extension.
Housekeeping of the nine Cap-Saint-Jacques buildings from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension until October 31, 2031.
Tree felling planned from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
For the night sky designation: lighting plan to be filed in February 2027, DarkSky response expected in April 2027, site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations to shelter people experiencing homelessness during the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. All three loans end on April 30, 2026.

etapes.titre: Warming centres and outreach workers in boroughs
etapes.texte: Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two psychosocial outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of a contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. to operate a warming centre for the 2025-2026 winter.

etapes.titre: Financial support for organizations over three years
etapes.texte: The City is granting $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and adding $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028. The projects deal with the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public space, and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Private donations and Bain Saint-Denis fit-up
etapes.texte: Urban agglomeration council adopts a framework for receiving private cash donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for fit-up work on the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis, and city council adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness.

etapes.titre: Encampments, support services and Nuit des sans-abri
etapes.texte: The City awards Mission Old Brewery a $149,520 contract to support people in the Notre-Dame street encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 judgment on the encampments under the Van Horne viaduct, and Ville-Marie regulates noise for the October 16, 2026 event on rue Beaudry.

aSurveiller.texte: The social brigade agreement with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
The ruling on the merits of the dispute over the encampments at the Van Horne viaduct is expected in 2027, according to the file.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City is renting to the Société de transport de Montréal a 2,787-square-metre lot south of rue de Louvain, for parking by employees with a sticker, for $49,293 over three years. It is also renting 836 square metres to a pay-by-app parking company, for $45,049 before taxes.

etapes.titre: Temporary uses of the Louvain Ouest lot
etapes.texte: The City is lending, free of charge, a 10,000-square-foot lot to an organization for a vegetable garden, and two parcels totalling 3,316 square metres to another organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. The borough is paying $35,000 to an organization for the Esplanade-Louvain pop-up space at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, is authorizing an event-related use on the vacant lot, and city council is taking on an activation lease on 78,244 square feet.

etapes.titre: The main street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the Louvain eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The file states that the first residential project is under construction and that addresses need to be assigned in the short term.

The City is awarding a company a contract worth $10,311,940.25 including taxes to build a street with sewer, water main, roadway, electrical network and lighting, for a total expenditure of $15,366,336. The contract includes the rehabilitation of the soil at the former gas station site, for which the City is adding $2,007,312.15 net to the infrastructure department's budget.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and the construction of a group of buildings, with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It is also adopting a draft by-law setting the height limit at 73 metres on part of the municipal lot, at the corner of avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: Work on rue de Louvain Est continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bump-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The Ministère des Transports' response to the financial assistance request is expected in fall 2026.
The loan of the lot for the greenhouse and sunflowers runs until October 31, 2027; the one for the vegetable garden, until December 31, 2027.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the time the development is completed, expected around 2032.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: The City is adjusting its residual materials collections: new days and new frequencies in several boroughs, purchase of bins, support for residents. It is extending contracts for food waste treatment, container collection and ecocentre service, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling its annual reports and reports from the inspector general on subcontracting in collection.

etapes.texte: The executive committee changes the days, schedules and collection zones in L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève and in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal. In Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, garbage is collected every two weeks from November 1 to April 30 and every week from May 1 to October 31, and the division of sectors 41 and 42 changes starting May 1, 2026.

The City extends twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanize food waste from the east of the agglomeration, at an additional cost of $3,269,055.43 taxes included per extension [CG26 0045]. It explains that the commissioning of the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre is not confirmed and that it can end the contracts with 30 days' notice [CG26 0417].

etapes.titre: Collection bins and information for residents
etapes.texte: The City enters into framework agreements to supply brown bins and garbage bins, then others to supply and distribute garbage bins in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where collection will be spaced out in two phases, fall 2026 and fall 2027 [CM26 0690]. Ahuntsic-Cartierville gives Ville en vert a mandate for information and awareness, and the executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris to loan reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations for neighbourhood events.

The City extends by 12 months the contracts for front-load and semi-underground container collection awarded to Waste Connections of Canada inc. / Enviro Connexions, as well as the container contract for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre transferred to GFL Environmental inc. It awards Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25 taxes included to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres [CG26 0416], extends the discharge authorization management software, and retains two firms for studies related to construction on former disposal sites.

aSurveiller.texte: The extension of food waste treatment by Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. runs until February 28, 2027.
Container collection and the container service at the Saint-Laurent ecocentre are maintained until October 31, 2027.
The loan of dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until December 31, 2026, at the latest.
The discharge authorization software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. This year, it obtained from the Gouvernement du Québec an additional delay to sell a first parcel of land, adopted two loan by-laws for the waterworks and public domain, and transferred a parcel of land to an organization for non-market housing. It is also leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Extended delay to sell a first parcel of land
etapes.texte: The Gouvernement du Québec grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first parcel of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The City approves the addendum to the 2017 deed of transfer, with no financial compensation.

The City guarantees a loan of $2,000,000 granted by the Canada Infrastructure Bank to Société GALOPH, to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, city council rejects an opposition motion on governance and asset management for the sector.

etapes.titre: Two loans for the waterworks and streets
etapes.texte: The City adopts a loan of $29,000,000 to develop the public domain of the neighbourhood: soils, sewers, waterworks, streets, land purchases. It also adopts a loan of $12,000,000 to build water main pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella.

The City leases parcels of the site to three organizations for $100 or $200 in rent: urban agriculture with MultiCaf and with the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora, transition nursery with the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain.

The City transfers, at no cost, to the organization Communia a vacant parcel of land of 4,777.7 square metres in the southeast part of the former racetrack, to build at least 225 non-market housing units there. It repeals the 2025 agreement with another organization and authorizes a depreciation expense of $877,488.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline granted to the City to complete the sale of a first parcel of land on the site.
2031: date by which the infrastructure must be completed, according to the condition of the federal grant cited in the loan by-laws.
April 30, 2027: end of the urban agriculture lease with MultiCaf.
March 31, 2028: end of the extended lease of the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora. April 30, 2028: end of the lease of the transition nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City funded studies, awarded design contracts and launched park redevelopment projects in several boroughs, from Le Sud-Ouest to Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, as well as Verdun, LaSalle and Saint-Laurent. It also adjusted contracts already underway, when contaminated soil or unforeseen site issues extended the work. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it repaired infrastructure, awarded routine maintenance work and submitted an application for an international designation related to the night sky.

etapes.texte: The City awarded the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the Bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included [CM26 0082]. It also paid money to Verdun for soil studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, accepted a sum from Hydro-Québec for phase 4 of parc d'Argenson, and authorized a public art competition at parc des Eaux-Cachées.

etapes.titre: Work and maintenance in the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The City awarded a contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, in the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub. It also awarded contracts for snow removal on service roads and parking lots, the felling of ash trees and declining trees, and janitorial maintenance of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector.

etapes.titre: New projects and land transferred to park status
etapes.texte: More redevelopment contracts were awarded: parcs Denise-Morelle and Baldwin in Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, parc J.O.R.-Leduc in LaSalle and parc Aimé-Caron in Saint-Laurent. The City also removed a portion of street from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension requested the same change for a 75.2-square-metre strip at parc Le Prévost.

aSurveiller.texte: The snow removal contract for the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers the period from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Janitorial maintenance of nine buildings in the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a 12-month extension option.
For the DarkSky application, the lighting management plan must be submitted in February 2027 and the response is expected in April 2027.
For the parc des Eaux-Cachées public art competition: winner selection in October 2026, contract in December 2026 and installation of the work in 2028.
Final acceptance of the work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027.
Work on parc J.O.R.-Leduc, in LaSalle, is expected to be completed in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial activity by-laws.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares: it adopts funding rules, pays out money to boroughs and commercial development corporations, then closes street sections to cars and regulates sales, noise and traffic on these streets. It also settles a dispute related to the development of a public square, changes the status of a piece of land, and names a square.

etapes.titre: Funding rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to the work on a public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer.

The boroughs close street sections to cars and authorize terraces, the sale of food and drinks, music and ground painting: Ville-Marie for thirteen streets, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce for the Placette CDN and avenues Royal and Madison, Outremont for avenue Bernard, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve for rue Ontario Est, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal for avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth.

The executive committee grants $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street from July 10 to 19, 2026, during the FIFA World Cup. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce closes avenue de Monkland for a commercial promotion from August 20 to 23, 2026, and Ville-Marie authorizes a musical sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles.

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque, in Montréal-Nord, "place Chez-Marguerite," and changes a 899-square-metre piece of land from street status to local park status near the Langelier metro station. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal in three sections.

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Traffic resumes on the chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges ramp on November 1, 2026, after dismantling on November 1 and 2.
The by-law on the sound ambiance of the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period until December 31, 2027; the 2027 edition will take place only if the pedestrianization project is renewed.
The pedestrianization assistance for avenue Lacombe continues until December 31, 2028: $22,500 in 2027 and $20,000 in 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève is requesting an additional six months, after a first extension obtained in July 2025.

Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, Ville-Marie is revising its rules on urban planning, special projects, demolition, certificates and cadastral operations. The by-law authorizes a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and allows public transit stations in category E.1 sectors.

The borough is changing the heights, uses and lot coverage ratio in the sector bordered by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est, and is increasing the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse. It is also amending its by-law on building demolition, following a public meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Laurent public consultation on its three draft by-laws, on October 20, 2026 at 7 p.m.
Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce: public consultation on October 21, 2026 and adoption on November 2, 2026; the deadline granted by the minister runs until December 16, 2026.
Saint-Léonard must adopt all its concordance by-laws by June 16, 2027, the date set by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville is requesting an extension until June 16, 2027.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.
L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève plans to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's police department (SPVM): contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The City adopts a loan by-law of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys patrol motorcycles, replaces the oil heating of the cavalry building at 1515, chemin Remembrance, and extends the housekeeping services at its headquarters. It also hands over meals for detained persons to a new company and extends the maintenance of the call dispatch system's software.

etapes.titre: Leases for neighbourhood stations and premises
etapes.texte: The City renews the leases for neighbourhood station 15, rue de l'Église in Verdun, and neighbourhood station 26, avenue Mountain Sights. It also rents 50 parking spaces at 260, boulevard De Maisonneuve and extends the lease of the SPVM training centre, rue Ernest-Cormier in Anjou.

aSurveiller.texte: October 23, 2026: "Fèves au lard" day of the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood station 46, for which the borough of Anjou bought tickets.
February 1, 2027: start of the ten-year lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.
March 1, 2027: deadline for delivery of the port patrol boat and its trailer.
September 30, 2027: expected completion of the work to replace the oil heating of the cavalry building.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and borrowings of the Société de transport de Montréal (STM), and sells, leases or lends it land for its stations, ventilation buildings and staff. It also oversees metro construction sites and bus stops on its territory, and entrusts the STM with municipal work related to the blue line extension. Borough councils and city council adopt motions on the development of the network.

etapes.titre: Bus stops and construction sites overseen
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville sets up and removes bus waiting areas as part of the network redesign, and Saint-Laurent offers to take charge of building sidewalks for new stops. Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to drill and rebuild the green line tunnel vault 24 hours a day from June 10 to July 31, 2026; the City signs an agreement to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation building in Outremont, adds an incidental budget to the Berri-UQAM station construction site, and does not object to the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes an expenditure of $3,808,451.29, taxes included. It then concludes 72-month master agreements with Artelia Canada inc. and Stantec Experts-conseils ltée for design, technical assistance and impact management for the redevelopment of the blue line corridor.

The agglomeration approves STM borrowings and amends its capital works program: analysis of replacing MR-73 cars, extending their service life, bus priority measures, Réno-Infrastructures phase 4, renovation of surface buildings, and management of technological and security risks.

City council asks Québec to study the conditions for keeping the tunnel boring machine used for the blue line in Montréal. Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles and LaSalle call for structuring public transit projects in the East and in the Grand Sud-Ouest, while Anjou asks the STM to stop studying a reserved lane on rue Beaubien and avenue du Val-d'Anjou.

aSurveiller.texte: Approval from the ministère des Affaires municipales expected in November 2026 for borrowings related to the MR-73 cars and the renovation of surface buildings.
Work on the Rielle ventilation building, in Verdun, is to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is expected to continue until March 2028.
The opening of the five new blue line stations is expected in 2031.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City and boroughs are building and repairing bike lanes, regulating car traffic around them, and buying equipment for the BIXI system. Work affects the REV Lajeunesse, rue Saint-Jacques, avenue Christophe-Colomb and corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. The City is also settling its rent with Hydro-Québec for land used as bike paths and asking Québec for financial help for four new projects.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes spending of $100,000, taxes included, for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is renting a mini sweeper with operator for the spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide.

Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is imposing mandatory manoeuvres on drivers on avenue Christophe-Colomb and making official the bike lanes between rue des Carrières and rue de Bellechasse. Outremont is tabling a draft by-law to turn a shared lane on avenue Lajoie into a one-way bike path, and Ville-Marie is making rue Saint-Jacques one-way eastbound between Peel and Robert-Bourassa for a section of the REV.

The City is awarding PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. a sole-source contract worth $4,815,802.61, taxes included, for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with BIXI, then a contract worth $394,851.17, taxes included, to Laser AMP for the steel bases of the stations. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Le Sud-Ouest are each including the installation of a BIXI station in street and laneway projects.

City council is approving an agreement worth $125,167.62, taxes included, for unpaid rent from 2014 to 2025 on Hydro-Québec land used for bike paths, parks and gardens. It is then approving a 10-year lease, starting January 1, 2026, for a strip of about 366 square metres used as a bike path in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial help from Québec
etapes.texte: The City is authorizing the filing of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable to build bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. It is committing to pay at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: The new traffic directions and lane assignments on rue Saint-Jacques, related to the REV, take effect on November 6, 2026.
The lease for the bike path land rented from Hydro-Québec in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until December 31, 2035.
